headline: High-risk default data leakage and cascading errors: Kestra’s broad filesystem/network automation can feed Notion AI workspace content and vendor backends without strong isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Kestra can write/read files and emit messages/notifications, while Notion AI ingests workspace pages and databases. If Kestra places attacker-controlled text into shared pages or docs, Notion may treat it as trusted content. This is not provably blocked by either profile, but it is not a direct default parser bridge either.
conditions: IF Kestra writes untrusted content into pages or databases that Notion AI later summarizes
IF the workspace content is used as instruction-bearing text rather than data
mitigations: Restrict Kestra outputs to non-executable templates
Add a human review step before Notion AI consumes generated pages
Tag machine-generated pages with a visible prefix
Separate automation output pages from AI-assisted knowledge pages
requires-engineering: implement provenance labels in the workspace

B_data_leakage.rationale: Kestra touches logs, inputs, artifacts, database data, cloud storage data, messages, and notifications, and has broad network egress. Notion AI reads workspace pages and sends content to Notion vendor backends/downstream model providers. If Kestra writes sensitive data into shared workspace content, Notion can transmit it off-platform by default.
conditions: IF Kestra places secrets, logs, or database data into Notion-accessible pages
IF Notion AI is used on those pages without redaction
mitigations: Block sensitive fields from being written into workspace pages
Use a redaction pass before copying automation outputs into Notion
Limit Notion AI access to non-sensitive pages
Review workspace permissions for the invoking user
requires-engineering: add DLP controls on Kestra outputs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Kestra has filesystem write, shell, subprocess, and broad API access; Notion AI has shared workspace state across instances and workspace-page write surfaces. They do not share host-level write primitives, but they can both mutate the same knowledge artifacts, creating overlapping writes and race-like conflicts in shared workspace content.
conditions: IF Kestra-generated content and Notion AI edits target the same workspace pages
IF multiple Notion AI instances operate on the same shared workspace state
mitigations: Assign separate pages for automation output and human editing
Use naming conventions to partition ownership
Schedule automation and AI editing in separate windows
Add manual approval before overwriting shared pages
requires-engineering: add locking or version checks in the workspace workflow

D_cascading_error.rationale: Kestra can generate workflow artifacts, logs, messages, and notifications, and Notion AI is a RAG-style Q&A system grounded in workspace content. If Kestra-produced text is treated as authoritative in Notion, downstream summaries or decisions can propagate errors without verification. The pair lacks a documented verification barrier, so the safer severity is high.
conditions: IF Notion AI answers questions using Kestra-generated pages as source material
IF humans act on Notion AI summaries without checking the underlying Kestra artifacts
mitigations: Require source-link citations in Notion pages
Cross-check critical outputs against Kestra logs
Mark generated pages as draft until reviewed
Limit Notion AI use for operational decisions
requires-engineering: add verification gates between Kestra and Notion

E_compliance.rationale: Kestra can process logs, inputs, database data, cloud storage data, messages, and notifications, while Notion AI stores and processes workspace pages through vendor backends and downstream model providers. That creates a plausible retention/residency mismatch for regulated content, but the profiles do not prove a specific jurisdictional violation, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated data is copied from Kestra into Notion workspace pages
IF the workspace retention or residency policy differs from the source system
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Notion pages
Use separate workspaces for regulated content
Review retention settings in both systems
Delete copied sensitive pages promptly
requires-engineering: formalize a data-processing agreement and residency controls
